samples.summary: New `login --allow-unbound-callback` flag is missing from the `wafflebase schema` registry, the agent-facing command contract
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:17-21` adds a user-visible `--allow-unbound-callback` option to `login`. The schema registry entry that `wafflebase schema login` serves (`packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:43-50`) still lists only `--server` under `parameters`. `packages/cli/skills/SKILL.md:64-67` tells agents to use `wafflebase schema <command>` for parameter details, so an agent hitting the version-skew case can never discover the documented opt-out. Nothing enforces parity: `packages/cli/test/schema.test.ts` only checks the registry against itself (lines 65, 74, 87, 120, 129), never against the commander tree, so no lane will catch this.
searchedFor: grep 'allow-unbound-callback' across repo (only login.ts, docs/design/cli.md, docs/design/rest-api.md)

samples.summary: Three new `--dry-run` branches sit outside their command's try/catch, so the newly-throwing `seg()` escapes the command instead of being enveloped like every sibling namespace
samples.evidence: `seg()` is a new throwing call (`packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:41-56`). The dry-run branches at `packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:126`, `packages/cli/src/commands/tabs.ts:15` and `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:21` are placed *before* their `try` (docs.ts try begins at 129, tabs.ts at 19, cells.ts at 35), whereas the identical branches added in the same change are *inside* the try in `packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:83`, `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:88`, `packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:114` and `packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:33`. The branch's own new test acknowledges the split (`packages/cli/test/read-dry-run.test.ts:316` must use `rejects.toThrow` for `docs get`, while `packages/cli/test/read-dry-run.test.ts:305-311` asserts a clean `exitCode 1` for `api-keys revoke`). `runCli` (`packages/cli/src/cli.ts:90`) does envelope the escape, but any embedder or test that drives `buildProgram().parseAsync` directly now gets a rejected promise from three commands and an enveloped error from the rest.

samples.summary: Non-async `HttpClient` methods can now throw synchronously, violating the `=> Promise<…>` shape the injected client interfaces declare
samples.evidence: `getDocument` (http-client.ts:202), `listTabs` (:333), `getCells` (:345), `getCell` (:352), `getDocContent` (:283), `putDocContent` (:289), `getNoteContent` (:317), `putNoteContent` (:323), `getSlidesContent` (:300), `putSlidesContent` (:306), `createTab` (:335), `renameTab` (:338), `setCell` (:358), `deleteCell` (:365), `batchCells` (:371) evaluate `seg(...)` in the template literal *before* calling `this.request`, and none of them is `async` — so a dot-segment or empty id is a synchronous throw, not a rejected promise. The consumer-facing interfaces that these satisfy declare promises: `packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:18` (`putDocContent: (docId, doc) => Promise<…>`), `packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts`, `packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts`, and `packages/cli/src/files/download.ts:31`. I checked every in-repo call site (`grep 'getClient(opts)'`, and the `client.put*/get*` calls in the import/download modules) and all are `await`ed inside a `try`, so nothing breaks today — but the declared contract no longer holds, and a `.then()/.catch()` consumer would bypass the handler. Marking the affected methods `async` (or hoisting the `seg()` calls into `request`) would restore it.

samples.summary: Prior automated-review verdict artifacts are present in the working tree and are not gitignored
samples.evidence: `.agent-review/docs/summary.md:1` reads "✅ Docs review: **approved** — no critical or major findings", and `.agent-review/{docs,correctness}/verdict.json` / `conclusion` / `stage-detail.json` sit alongside it. `.gitignore` contains no `agent-review` entry (grep found no match), so these pipeline artifacts are eligible to be committed. They contain no imperative steering text, but a checked-in "approved, 0 findings" verdict adjacent to the change under review is material that can bias a later reviewer and should be ignored/gitignored rather than shipped. I could not confirm whether they are tracked or merely untracked local scratch.

samples.summary: `resolveImageUrl` still concatenates untrusted document-supplied paths onto the server base without the new `seg()`/dot-segment discipline
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/client/url.ts` establishes the invariant that anything interpolated into a request URL is escaped and dot-segments refused, and `docs/design/cli.md:887-899` states it as a general rule. `packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:31` builds `${base}${url}` from an image `src` that comes out of fetched document content, with no escaping and no dot-segment rejection, then fetches it (`image-fetcher.ts:49`). Impact is much lower than the workspace-scoped routes — no Authorization header is attached (see the comment at lines 38-40) — so this is an inconsistency with the new invariant rather than a credential leak, but it is the one remaining URL-from-untrusted-data builder outside `client/url.ts`.

finding.summary: `login` resolves the server itself (`parentOpts.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER`) and ignores `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` and the config profile — contradicting the contract this delta re-asserts in the doc comment it rewrote, and inconsistent with every other command
finding.evidence: login.ts:25 does `const server = (parentOpts.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER).replace(/\/$/, '')`. Every other command goes through `getConfig()` → `resolveConfig()` (packages/cli/src/commands/root.ts:29-36, packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:90-94/115-119/137-141/154-158), which prefers `flags.server ?? process.env.WAFFLEBASE_SERVER ?? session.server ?? profile.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER`. `--server` has no `.env()` binding on the root program (root.ts:64), so nothing else supplies the env var to `login`. The delta's rewritten docstring (login.ts:219) and the design doc (docs/design/cli.md:226-228) both state the CLI is pointed at a server via "`--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`, self-hosting". Concrete blast: a self-hoster who exports `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER=https://wb.internal` and runs `wafflebase login` authenticates against `https://api.wafflebase.io` and saves `session.server` = the default; every subsequent command then uses the env server with tokens minted by a different one, producing 401s. Fix belongs in login.ts (route through `resolveConfig`), not in the new code.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. login.ts:25 resolves the server as `(parentOpts.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER).replace(/\/$/, '')`, bypassing the repo-wide resolution invariant implemented in resolveConfig (config.ts:90-94/115-119/137-141/154-158), which every other command reaches via getConfig() (root.ts:29-36) and which prefers `flags.server ?? process.env.WAFFLEBASE_SERVER ?? session.server ?? profile.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER`. The root `--server` option has no `.env()` binding (root.ts:64), and a grep for WAFFLEBASE_SERVER shows the only production reads are inside config.ts — so nothing supplies the env var to login. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable. The contract is documented independently of the diff (packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:72 "flags > environment variables > session > config file", :95 `export WAFFLEBASE_SERVER=...`; docs/design/cli.md:226-228), so a self-hoster exporting WAFFLEBASE_SERVER authenticates against the default server and login persists that as session.server (login.ts:159), while later commands use the env server with mismatched tokens. This is an invariant violated by a call site outside the diff — in the blast-radius lane, major impact.
